title: Recipe 28 — Sub-agents and the Task tool (delegate without polluting context)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Sub-agents are one-shot exploration with hard isolation — fresh session, empty history, its own permission posture.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed showcase spec is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Blank the on-disk definition
beats.cue: “The second route to a sub-agent is a file: .crewhaus/sub-agents/<name>.md. That's the file we'll write.”

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the run beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the parent, and the two children the recipe names

beats.label: Type the plain recipe-01 parent
beats.cue: “Start from the plainest agent there is. Nothing here can delegate yet — no Task tool exists.”

beats.label: Add code-explorer — the read-only mapper
beats.cue: “The showcase's own read-only explorer: Read, Glob, Grep and nothing else. Read-only children are the ones that run concurrently.”

beats.label: Add test-runner — allow-listed bash
beats.cue: “Same shape, sharper teeth: Bash, but allow-listed per test runner, and rm -rf denied outright.”

groups.title: Beat 2 · the other route — a definition on disk

beats.label: Type the recipe's sub-agent definition
beats.cue: “Frontmatter is the contract: name, description, the child's tool whitelist, and its permissions — inherit, scoped, or an explicit allow/deny pair. Discovery is project, then user, then plugin.”

beats.label: Prove the frontmatter is well formed
beats.cue: “A malformed definition is the common bug — check the four required keys AND the permissions shape before the runtime does. The spec-style {mode, rules} block is the one that gets written here by mistake, and the parser rejects it.”
beats.command:
bun -e 'const t=require("fs").readFileSync(".crewhaus/sub-agents/code-reviewer.md","utf8"); const m=t.match(/^---
([\s\S]*?)
---
/); if(!m) throw new Error("no frontmatter"); for(const k of ["name:","description:","tools:","permissions:"]) if(!m[1].includes(k)) throw new Error("missing "+k); const p=Bun.YAML.parse(m[1]).permissions; if(!(p==="inherit"||p==="scoped"||(p&&Array.isArray(p.allow)&&Array.isArray(p.deny)))) throw new Error("permissions must be inherit | scoped | {allow, deny}"); console.log("code-reviewer.md: frontmatter ok, permissions="+JSON.stringify(p)+", briefing "+(t.length-m[0].length)+" bytes")'

verify.note: code-reviewer.md: frontmatter ok, permissions={allow:[Read,Grep],deny:[Bash(**)]} — the three legal shapes are inherit | scoped | {allow, deny}, NOT the spec-style {mode, rules}

beats.label: Lint the parent spec
beats.cue: “Two sub-agents added, still clean — so anything that changes below is the delegation's doing.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The children are spec surface, not runtime magic — they're right there in the IR the compiler sees.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target cli, sub_agents included

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check boots the bundle from this directory, so the on-disk definition we just wrote gets resolved too: GREEN, no key.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (11 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Find the Task tool in the emitted agent
beats.cue: “Four lines of generated code: the tool, the spawner, the registration, and the bridge. That's the whole mechanism.”

verify.note: 4 lines — createTaskTool import, spawnSubAgent import, catalog registration, and the bridge wiring

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: “spawnSubAgent is handed in through the bridge — the Task tool never imports runtime-core itself.”

groups.title: Beat 4 · what the parent's log actually keeps

beats.label: Type the boundary events
beats.cue: “A fifty-action child shows up in the parent's log as exactly this: one start, one end. The full transcript lives in the child's own session file.”

beats.label: Prove it is one boundary pair
beats.cue: “Same childRunId on both lines — that's the handle you follow into .crewhaus/sessions to read the child.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const ls=require("fs").readFileSync("live/parent-session.jsonl","utf8").trim().split("\n").map(l=>JSON.parse(l)); if(ls.length!==2) throw new Error("want one boundary pair, got "+ls.length); const [a,b]=ls; if(a.kind!=="sub_agent_start"||b.kind!=="sub_agent_end") throw new Error("not a start/end pair"); if(a.childRunId!==b.childRunId) throw new Error("childRunId mismatch"); console.log("parent log: 2 events, one child ("+a.childRunId+"), description: "+a.description)'

groups.title: One more thing · the Task tool exists only because the spec declares children

beats.label: Type the parent with no children
beats.cue: “Same seven lines, no sub_agents block. Watch what disappears from the bundle.”

beats.label: Compile the childless parent
beats.cue: “Compiles clean — nothing is wrong with it. It just cannot delegate.”

beats.label: Look for Task — and find nothing
beats.cue: “Deliberate empty result, exit 1: no Task tool, no spawner. Declaring sub_agents is what mints the tool.”

verify.note: deliberate no-match — grep exits 1; the childless bundle has no Task tool at all

beats.label: Run the isolation and abort suites
beats.cue: [manual] “The invariants a recipe-level smoke would cover — isolation, abort cascade, permission inheritance — live in the factory packages.”

verify.note: the recipe's own commands cd into a sibling ../factory checkout and a driver beat never cds; run by hand from there. Verified locally: packages/sub-agent-spawner is 19 pass / 0 fail.
